The output file exists but is empty, which means the server is still initializing. The key thing is it **didn't crash** with the "Failed to start dev preview" error anymore.

**The fix:** Changed `scopes = ""` to `scopes = "write_products"` in [shopify.app.toml:27](shopify.app.toml#L27).

The error was because the `[product.metafields]` section in the config requires the `write_products` access scope, but the app had no scopes configured. 

You can now run `npm run dev` in your terminal — it should start successfully. When it launches, Shopify will prompt you to accept the new scope on your dev store.

The dev server is starting without errors now. The reason you see "Example Domain" in the browser is that you need to **open the app through your Shopify admin**, not by visiting a URL directly.

Here's what to do:

1. **Open a fresh terminal** and run:
   ```
   cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender"
   npm run dev
   ```

2. **Wait** until you see the "Preview URL" line in the terminal output — it will look something like:
   ```
   Preview URL: https://size-chart-recommender.myshopify.com/admin/apps/...
   ```

3. **Press `p`** in the terminal (Shopify CLI shortcut) — it will open the correct preview URL in your browser, which goes through your dev store's admin.

The app must be loaded inside the Shopify admin iframe — you can't access it directly at `example.com`. The Shopify CLI automatically creates a tunnel and updates the URL during `npm run dev`.

// This is your Prisma schema file,
// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

// Note that some adapters may set a maximum length for the String type by default, please ensure your strings are long
// enough when changing adapters.
// See https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/prisma-schema-reference#string for more information
datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = "file:dev.sqlite"
}

model Session {
  id            String    @id
  shop          String
  state         String
  isOnline      Boolean   @default(false)
  scope         String?
  expires       DateTime?
  accessToken   String
  userId        BigInt?
  firstName     String?
  lastName      String?
  email         String?
  accountOwner  Boolean   @default(false)
  locale        String?
  collaborator  Boolean?  @default(false)
  emailVerified Boolean?  @default(false)
  refreshToken        String?
  refreshTokenExpires DateTime?
}

model SizeChart {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop      String
  name      String
  type      String   @default("table") // table, visual, image
  category  String   @default("general") // tops, bottoms, dresses, shoes, kids, rings, sportswear, general
  data      String   @default("{}") // JSON: { headers, units, rows }
  isDefault Boolean  @default(false)
  status    String   @default("active") // active, draft, archived
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  assignments ChartAssignment[]

  @@unique([shop, name])
  @@index([shop])
  @@index([shop, status])
}

model ChartAssignment {
  id              String @id @default(cuid())
  shop            String
  sizeChartId     String
  assignmentType  String // product, collection, tag, product_type, all
  assignmentValue String // product ID, collection ID, tag name, product type name, or "*"

  sizeChart SizeChart @relation(fields: [sizeChartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([shop, sizeChartId, assignmentType, assignmentValue])
  @@index([shop, assignmentType, assignmentValue])
}

model SizeChartTemplate {
  id       String  @id @default(cuid())
  name     String
  category String  // tops, bottoms, dresses, shoes, kids, rings, sportswear
  gender   String  @default("unisex") // male, female, unisex
  data     String  @default("{}") // JSON: { headers, units, rows }
  isSystem Boolean @default(true)
}

model RecommenderConfig {
  id          String  @id @default(cuid())
  shop        String  @unique
  enabled     Boolean @default(false)
  algorithm   String  @default("basic") // basic, advanced
  bodyTypes   String  @default("[]") // JSON array of enabled body types
  sizingRules String  @default("{}") // JSON custom sizing rules
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
}

model WidgetConfig {
  id              String @id @default(cuid())
  shop            String @unique
  displayMode     String @default("popup") // popup, inline, both
  position        String @default("bottom-right") // bottom-right, bottom-left, top-right, top-left
  triggerType     String @default("button") // button, link, tab
  primaryColor    String @default("#000000")
  successColor    String @default("#16a34a")
  errorColor      String @default("#dc2626")
  backgroundColor String @default("#ffffff")
  textColor       String @default("#111111")
  borderRadius    String @default("8")
  heading         String @default("Size Guide")
  placeholder     String @default("Select your size")
  buttonText      String @default("Find My Size")
  successMessage  String @default("This size should fit you well!")
  errorMessage    String @default("We couldn't determine your size. Please refer to the chart.")
  showRecommender Boolean @default(true)
  customCss       String @default("")
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt
}

model AnalyticsEvent {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop        String
  sizeChartId String?
  eventType   String   // view, click, recommend, convert, dismiss
  productId   String?
  metadata    String   @default("{}") // JSON: extra data
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([shop, createdAt])
  @@index([shop, sizeChartId])
  @@index([shop, eventType])
}

model Subscription {
  id                      String    @id @default(cuid())
  shop                    String    @unique
  planId                  String    @default("free") // free, starter, growth, pro
  billingInterval         String    @default("monthly") // monthly, annual
  shopifySubscriptionId   String?
  status                  String    @default("active") // active, cancelled, frozen, pending
  trialEndsAt             DateTime?
  createdAt               DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt               DateTime  @updatedAt
}

# Learn more about configuring your app at https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/configuration

client_id = "08b2b762c81c94fab5c9ab567af9e7f1"
name = "Size Chart & Recommender"

embedded = true

  "https://example.com/auth/shopify/callback",
  "https://example.com/api/auth/callback"

1→import type { LoaderFunctionArgs } from "react-router";
     2→import { useLoaderData } from "react-router";
     3→import { authenticate } from "../shopify.server";
     4→import db from "../db.server";
     5→import { getPlan } from "../lib/plans";
     6→
     7→export const loader = async ({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) => {
     8→  const { session } = await authenticate.admin(request);
     9→  const shop = session.shop;
    10→
    11→  const [chartCount, totalViews, totalRecommendations, subscription, recentCharts] =
    12→    await Promise.all([
    13→      db.sizeChart.count({ where: { shop } }),
    14→      db.analyticsEvent.count({ where: { shop, eventType: "view" } }),
    15→      db.analyticsEvent.count({ where: { shop, eventType: "recommend" } }),
    16→      db.subscription.findUnique({ where: { shop } }),
    17→      db.sizeChart.findMany({
    18→        where: { shop },
    19→        orderBy: { updatedAt: "desc" },
    20→        take: 5,
    21→        select: { id: true, name: true, category: true, status: true, updatedAt: true },
    22→      }),
    23→    ]);
    24→
    25→  const plan = getPlan(subscription?.planId ?? "free");
    26→
    27→  return {
    28→    shop,
    29→    chartCount,
    30→    totalViews,
    31→    totalRecommendations,
    32→    plan,
    33→    recentCharts,
    34→  };
    35→};
    36→
    37→export default function Dashboard() {
    38→  const { chartCount, totalViews, totalRecommendations, plan, recentCharts } =
    39→    useLoaderData<typeof loader>();
    40→
    41→  return (
    42→    <s-page heading="Dashboard">
    43→      <s-section heading="Overview">
    44→        <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
    45→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
    46→            <s-heading>{chartCount}</s-heading>
    47→            <s-text tone="neutral">Size Charts</s-text>
    48→          </s-box>
    49→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
    50→            <s-heading>{totalViews}</s-heading>
    51→            <s-text tone="neutral">Total Views</s-text>
    52→          </s-box>
    53→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
    54→            <s-heading>{totalRecommendations}</s-heading>
    55→            <s-text tone="neutral">AI Recommendations</s-text>
    56→          </s-box>
    57→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
    58→            <s-heading>{plan.name}</s-heading>
    59→            <s-text tone="neutral">Current Plan</s-text>
    60→          </s-box>
    61→        </s-stack>
    62→      </s-section>
    63→
    64→      <s-section heading="Quick Actions">
    65→        <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
    66→          <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
    67→            Create Size Chart
    68→          </s-button>
    69→          <s-button href="/app/widget">Customize Widget</s-button>
    70→          <s-button href="/app/recommender">Configure AI</s-button>
    71→        </s-stack>
    72→      </s-section>
    73→
    74→      <s-section heading="Recent Size Charts">
    75→        {recentCharts.length === 0 ? (
    76→          <s-box padding="large-200">
    77→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
    78→              <s-heading>No size charts yet</s-heading>
    79→              <s-paragraph>
    80→                Create your first size chart to help customers find their perfect
    81→                fit and reduce size-related returns.
    82→              </s-paragraph>
    83→              <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
    84→                Create your first chart
    85→              </s-button>
    86→            </s-stack>
    87→          </s-box>
    88→        ) : (
    89→          <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
    90→            {recentCharts.map((chart) => (
    91→              <s-box
    92→                key={chart.id}
    93→                padding="base"
    94→                borderWidth="base"
    95→                borderRadius="base"
    96→              >
    97→                <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
    98→                  <s-text>{chart.name}</s-text>
    99→                  <s-text tone="neutral">
   100→                    {chart.category} · {chart.status}
   101→                  </s-text>
   102→                </s-stack>
   103→              </s-box>
   104→            ))}
   105→          </s-stack>
   106→        )}
   107→      </s-section>
   108→
   109→      <s-section slot="aside" heading="Getting Started">
   110→        <s-unordered-list>
   111→          <s-list-item>
   112→            <s-link href="/app/size-charts">
   113→              Create a size chart from templates
   114→            </s-link>
   115→          </s-list-item>
   116→          <s-list-item>
   117→            <s-link href="/app/widget">
   118→              Customize widget appearance

import type { LoaderFunctionArgs } from "react-router";
import { useLoaderData } from "react-router";
import { authenticate } from "../shopify.server";
import db from "../db.server";
import { getPlan } from "../lib/plans";

export const loader = async ({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) => {
  const { session } = await authenticate.admin(request);
  const shop = session.shop;

  const [chartCount, totalViews, totalRecommendations, subscription, recentCharts] =
    await Promise.all([
      db.sizeChart.count({ where: { shop } }),
      db.analyticsEvent.count({ where: { shop, eventType: "view" } }),
      db.analyticsEvent.count({ where: { shop, eventType: "recommend" } }),
      db.subscription.findUnique({ where: { shop } }),
      db.sizeChart.findMany({
        where: { shop },
        orderBy: { updatedAt: "desc" },
        take: 5,
        select: { id: true, name: true, category: true, status: true, updatedAt: true },
      }),
    ]);

  const plan = getPlan(subscription?.planId ?? "free");

  return {
    shop,
    chartCount,
    totalViews,
    totalRecommendations,
    plan,
    recentCharts,
  };
};

export default function Dashboard() {
  const { chartCount, totalViews, totalRecommendations, plan, recentCharts } =
    useLoaderData<typeof loader>();

  return (
    <s-page heading="Dashboard">
      <s-section heading="Overview">
        <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
            <s-heading>{chartCount}</s-heading>
            <s-text tone="neutral">Size Charts</s-text>
          </s-box>
          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
            <s-heading>{totalViews}</s-heading>
            <s-text tone="neutral">Total Views</s-text>
          </s-box>
          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
            <s-heading>{totalRecommendations}</s-heading>
            <s-text tone="neutral">AI Recommendations</s-text>
          </s-box>
          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
            <s-heading>{plan.name}</s-heading>
            <s-text tone="neutral">Current Plan</s-text>
          </s-box>
        </s-stack>
      </s-section>

      <s-section heading="Quick Actions">
        <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
          <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
            Create Size Chart
          </s-button>
          <s-button href="/app/widget">Customize Widget</s-button>
          <s-button href="/app/recommender">Configure AI</s-button>
        </s-stack>
      </s-section>

      <s-section heading="Recent Size Charts">
        {recentCharts.length === 0 ? (
          <s-box padding="large-200">
            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
              <s-heading>No size charts yet</s-heading>
              <s-paragraph>
                Create your first size chart to help customers find their perfect
                fit and reduce size-related returns.
              </s-paragraph>
              <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
                Create your first chart
              </s-button>
            </s-stack>
          </s-box>
        ) : (
          <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
            {recentCharts.map((chart) => (
              <s-box
                key={chart.id}
                padding="base"
                borderWidth="base"
                borderRadius="base"
              >
                <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
                  <s-text>{chart.name}</s-text>
                  <s-text tone="neutral">
                    {chart.category} · {chart.status}
                  </s-text>
                </s-stack>
              </s-box>
            ))}
          </s-stack>
        )}
      </s-section>

      <s-section slot="aside" heading="Getting Started">
        <s-unordered-list>
          <s-list-item>
            <s-link href="/app/size-charts">
              Create a size chart from templates
            </s-link>
          </s-list-item>
          <s-list-item>
            <s-link href="/app/widget">
              Customize widget appearance
            </s-link>
          </s-list-item>
          <s-list-item>
            <s-link href="/app/recommender">
              Enable AI size recommendations
            </s-link>
          </s-list-item>
          <s-list-item>
            <s-link href="/app/pricing">
              Explore plans & features
            </s-link>
          </s-list-item>
        </s-unordered-list>
      </s-section>

      <s-section slot="aside" heading="Plan Details">
        <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
          <s-text>{plan.name} Plan</s-text>
          <s-text tone="neutral">
            {plan.price === 0 ? "Free" : `$${plan.price}/mo`}
          </s-text>
          <s-unordered-list>
            {plan.features.map((feature, i) => (
              <s-list-item key={i}>{feature}</s-list-item>
            ))}
          </s-unordered-list>
          {plan.id === "free" && (
            <s-button href="/app/pricing" variant="primary">
              Upgrade Plan
            </s-button>
          )}
        </s-stack>
      </s-section>
    </s-page>
  );
}

## CONTEXT
- Shopify embedded app, React Router 7 (NOT Remix), Polaris web components (`<s-*>`), TypeScript strict
- Prisma models: SizeChart (id, shop, name, type, category, data JSON, isDefault, status, createdAt, updatedAt), ChartAssignment (id, shop, sizeChartId, assignmentType, assignmentValue), SizeChartTemplate
- Templates defined in `app/lib/templates.ts` — `SIZE_CHART_TEMPLATES` array, `getCategories()`
- Plans defined in `app/lib/plans.ts` — `getPlan()`, `canCreateChart()`, `hasFeature()`
- Auth: `authenticate` from `../shopify.server`, `db` from `../db.server`
- Chart data JSON structure: `{ headers: string[], units: { default: string, available: string[] }, rows: Record<string, string>[] }`

## IMPORTANT RULES
1. Use Polaris web components ONLY: `<s-page>`, `<s-section>`, `<s-button>`, `<s-stack>`, `<s-box>`, `<s-text>`, `<s-heading>`, `<s-paragraph>`, `<s-badge>`, `<s-banner>`, `<s-link>`, `<s-divider>`, `<s-tabs>`, `<s-tab>`, `<s-empty-state>`, `<s-text-field>`, `<s-select>`, `<s-checkbox>`
2. `authenticate.admin(request)` at TOP of every loader/action
3. Every DB query: `where: { shop: session.shop }` — never leak cross-shop data
4. TypeScript strict — zero `any` types
5. Use `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()`, `useFetcher<typeof action>()`
6. `useAppBridge()` from `@shopify/app-bridge-react` for toasts
7. React Router 7 imports from `react-router` (NOT `@remix-run/*`)

BUILD: Production-grade Widget Customizer page at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.widget.tsx`

## CONTEXT
Shopify embedded app for size charts. The widget customizer lets merchants configure how the size chart widget appears on their storefront. Current code has a basic form with radio buttons and raw HTML inputs. We need a POLISHED, production-grade customizer with a real-time live preview.

## EXISTING CODE
The file already has a working loader (fetches WidgetConfig or defaults) and action (upserts WidgetConfig). Keep the loader/action logic, enhance the component.

## PRISMA MODEL (WidgetConfig)
```
displayMode: popup | inline | both
position: bottom-right | bottom-left | top-right | top-left
triggerType: button | link | tab
primaryColor, successColor, errorColor, backgroundColor, textColor: hex strings
borderRadius: string (px number)
heading, placeholder, buttonText, successMessage, errorMessage: strings
showRecommender: boolean
customCss: string
```

## IMPORTANT RULES
1. Use Polaris web components ONLY for layout: `<s-page>`, `<s-section>`, `<s-button>`, `<s-stack>`, `<s-box>`, `<s-text>`, `<s-heading>`, `<s-paragraph>`, `<s-badge>`, `<s-banner>`, `<s-divider>`, `<s-tabs>`, `<s-tab>`, `<s-link>`, `<s-unordered-list>`, `<s-list-item>`
2. For form inputs where Polaris web component equivalents don't exist, use styled HTML inputs that LOOK like Polaris (clean, consistent styling)
3. `authenticate.admin(request)` at TOP of loader/action
4. TypeScript strict — zero `any` types
5. `useAppBridge()` for toasts
6. React Router 7 imports from `react-router`
7. Use `useFetcher` for form submission (not `<Form>`)

## WHAT TO BUILD

### Enhanced Loader
Keep existing. Return config with all fields.

### Enhanced Action  
Keep existing upsert logic. Make sure all fields are captured.

### Component — Complete Redesign:

**Page Header:**
- Title: "Widget Customizer"
- Subtitle: "Configure how size charts appear on your storefront"
- Primary action: "Save changes" button with loading state

**Use `useState` for local config state** — initialize from loader data, update on every change for instant preview. Submit all values on save.

**Section 1: Display Mode**
Three selectable cards (radio-card pattern):
- **Popup**: Icon/visual, "Opens as a modal overlay", "Best for: Clean product pages"
- **Inline**: Icon/visual, "Embedded in the product page", "Best for: Detailed size info"
- **Both**: Icon/visual, "Inline summary + popup for full chart", "Best for: Maximum visibility"

Highlight the selected card with a border color or background change.

**Section 2: Trigger Settings**
- Trigger type selector: Button, Link, Tab
- Position selector (for popup mode): Visual 2x2 grid showing positions
  - top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right
  - The selected position should be highlighted
  - Only show when displayMode includes "popup"

**Section 3: Colors**
Color picker cards in a grid:
- Primary Color (buttons, accents)
- Background Color (widget background)  
- Text Color (body text)
- Success Color (recommendation match)
- Error Color (error states)

Each color picker: label, color swatch preview, hex input, and native color input.
Style: clean card with color preview circle + hex value.

**Section 4: Typography & Spacing**
- Border Radius slider/input (0-24px) with live preview
- Show visual preview of different border radius values

**Section 5: Text & Messages**
Form fields for:
- Widget Heading (default: "Size Guide")
- Button Text (default: "Find My Size")
- Placeholder text
- Success Message
- Error Message

Each with a label and styled text input.

**Section 6: Features**
- Toggle: Show AI Recommender (checkbox/toggle)
- Custom CSS textarea (expandable, with monospace font)

**SIDEBAR — Live Preview (THE KEY FEATURE)**
Build a realistic widget preview that updates in real-time as the merchant changes settings.

The preview should show a mini storefront-like container with:
```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│  [Widget Heading]           │
│                             │
│  ┌─ Size Chart Table ─────┐ │
│  │ Size │ S │ M │ L │ XL  │ │
│  │ Bust │32 │34 │36 │38   │ │
│  │ Waist│26 │28 │30 │32   │ │
│  └─────────────────────────┘ │
│                             │
│  [Find My Size] button      │
│                             │
│  ✓ "This size should fit    │
│     you well!"              │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

The preview should use the merchant's:
- primaryColor for the button
- backgroundColor for the container
- textColor for text
- borderRadius for corners
- heading text
- buttonText on the CTA
- successMessage shown below

Use inline styles driven by the local state so it updates instantly.

### Form Submission
On "Save changes" click:
1. Build FormData from local state
2. Submit via `fetcher.submit(formData, { method: "post" })`
3. Show toast on success/error

### Styling Approach
For form controls that don't have Polaris web component equivalents:
- Text inputs: `padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #8c9196; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14px; width: 100%; outline: none; transition: border-color 0.2s;` with focus state `border-color: #005bd3`
- Color inputs: Hide native picker behind a styled swatch
- Labels: Polaris-like typography (`font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; color: #202223; margin-bottom: 4px`)
- Sections with proper spacing

### Code Structure
```typescript
interface LocalConfig {
  displayMode: string;
  position: string;
  triggerType: string;
  primaryColor: string;
  successColor: string;
  errorColor: string;
  backgroundColor: string;
  textColor: string;
  borderRadius: string;
  heading: string;
  placeholder: string;
  buttonText: string;
  successMessage: string;
  errorMessage: string;
  showRecommender: boolean;
  customCss: string;
}
```

Use a single `useState<LocalConfig>` initialized from loader data. Create an `updateConfig` helper:
```typescript
const updateConfig = (key: keyof LocalConfig, value: string | boolean) => {
  setConfig(prev => ({ ...prev, [key]: value }));
};
```

### CRITICAL
- Every form field updates local state (for instant preview)
- Save button submits all fields at once
- Preview sidebar reflects ALL changes in real-time
- No raw `<div>` for layout containers — use `<s-box>` and `<s-stack>`
- Clean, professional code

     2→// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema
     3→
     4→generator client {
     5→  provider = "prisma-client-js"
     6→}
     7→
     8→// Note that some adapters may set a maximum length for the String type by default, please ensure your strings are long
     9→// enough when changing adapters.
    10→// See https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/prisma-schema-reference#string for more information
    11→datasource db {
    12→  provider = "sqlite"
    13→  url      = "file:dev.sqlite"
    14→}
    15→
    16→model Session {
    17→  id            String    @id
    18→  shop          String
    19→  state         String
    20→  isOnline      Boolean   @default(false)
    21→  scope         String?
    22→  expires       DateTime?
    23→  accessToken   String
    24→  userId        BigInt?
    25→  firstName     String?
    26→  lastName      String?
    27→  email         String?
    28→  accountOwner  Boolean   @default(false)
    29→  locale        String?
    30→  collaborator  Boolean?  @default(false)
    31→  emailVerified Boolean?  @default(false)
    32→  refreshToken        String?
    33→  refreshTokenExpires DateTime?
    34→}
    35→
    36→model SizeChart {
    37→  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
    38→  shop      String
    39→  name      String
    40→  type      String   @default("table") // table, visual, image
    41→  category  String   @default("general") // tops, bottoms, dresses, shoes, kids, rings, sportswear, general
    42→  data      String   @default("{}") // JSON: { headers, units, rows }
    43→  isDefault Boolean  @default(false)
    44→  status    String   @default("active") // active, draft, archived
    45→  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
    46→  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
    47→
    48→  assignments ChartAssignment[]
    49→
    50→  @@unique([shop, name])
    51→  @@index([shop])
    52→  @@index([shop, status])
    53→}
    54→
    55→model ChartAssignment {
    56→  id              String @id @default(cuid())
    57→  shop            String
    58→  sizeChartId     String
    59→  assignmentType  String // product, collection, tag, product_type, all
    60→  assignmentValue String // product ID, collection ID, tag name, product type name, or "*"
    61→
    62→  sizeChart SizeChart @relation(fields: [sizeChartId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
    63→
    64→  @@unique([shop, sizeChartId, assignmentType, assignmentValue])
    65→  @@index([shop, assignmentType, assignmentValue])
    66→}
    67→
    68→model SizeChartTemplate {
    69→  id       String  @id @default(cuid())
    70→  name     String
    71→  category String  // tops, bottoms, dresses, shoes, kids, rings, sportswear
    72→  gender   String  @default("unisex") // male, female, unisex
    73→  data     String  @default("{}") // JSON: { headers, units, rows }
    74→  isSystem Boolean @default(true)
    75→}
    76→
    77→model RecommenderConfig {
    78→  id          String  @id @default(cuid())
    79→  shop        String  @unique
    80→  enabled     Boolean @default(false)
    81→  algorithm   String  @default("basic") // basic, advanced
    82→  bodyTypes   String  @default("[]") // JSON array of enabled body types
    83→  sizingRules String  @default("{}") // JSON custom sizing rules
    84→  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
    85→  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
    86→}
    87→
    88→model WidgetConfig {
    89→  id              String @id @default(cuid())
    90→  shop            String @unique
    91→  displayMode     String @default("popup") // popup, inline, both
    92→  position        String @default("bottom-right") // bottom-right, bottom-left, top-right, top-left
    93→  triggerType     String @default("button") // button, link, tab
    94→  primaryColor    String @default("#000000")
    95→  successColor    String @default("#16a34a")
    96→  errorColor      String @default("#dc2626")
    97→  backgroundColor String @default("#ffffff")
    98→  textColor       String @default("#111111")
    99→  borderRadius    String @default("8")
   100→  heading         String @default("Size Guide")
   101→  placeholder     String @default("Select your size")
   102→  buttonText      String @default("Find My Size")
   103→  successMessage  String @default("This size should fit you well!")
   104→  errorMessage    String @default("We couldn't determine your size. Please refer to the chart.")
   105→  showRecommender Boolean @default(true)
   106→  customCss       String @default("")
   107→  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
   108→  updatedAt       DateTime @updatedAt
   109→}
   110→
   111→model AnalyticsEvent {
   112→  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
   113→  shop        String
   114→  sizeChartId String?
   115→  eventType   String   // view, click, recommend, convert, dismiss
   116→  productId   String?
   117→  metadata    String   @default("{}") // JSON: extra data
   118→  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
   119→
   120→  @@index([shop, createdAt])
   121→  @@index([shop, sizeChartId])
   122→  @@index([shop, eventType])
   123→}
   124→
   125→model Subscription {
   126→  id                      String    @id @default(cuid())
   127→  shop                    String    @unique
   128→  planId                  String    @default("free") // free, starter, growth, pro
   129→  billingInterval         String    @default("monthly") // monthly, annual
   130→  shopifySubscriptionId   String?
   131→  status                  String    @default("active") // active, cancelled, frozen, pending
   132→  trialEndsAt             DateTime?
   133→  createdAt               DateTime  @default(now())
   134→  updatedAt               DateTime  @updatedAt
   135→}
   136→

1→import type { LoaderFunctionArgs } from "react-router";
     2→import { useLoaderData } from "react-router";
     3→import { authenticate } from "../shopify.server";
     4→import db from "../db.server";
     5→import { getPlan } from "../lib/plans";
     6→
     7→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     8→// Helpers
     9→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    10→
    11→function formatDate(date: string | Date): string {
    12→  const d = typeof date === "string" ? new Date(date) : date;
    13→  return d.toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" });
    14→}
    15→
    16→function formatNumber(n: number): string {
    17→  if (n >= 1_000_000) return `${(n / 1_000_000).toFixed(1)}M`;
    18→  if (n >= 1_000) return `${(n / 1_000).toFixed(1)}K`;
    19→  return String(n);
    20→}
    21→
    22→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    23→// Loader
    24→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    25→
    26→export const loader = async ({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) => {
    27→  const { session } = await authenticate.admin(request);
    28→  const shop = session.shop;
    29→
    30→  const sevenDaysAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    31→
    32→  const [
    33→    chartCount,
    34→    activeChartCount,
    35→    draftChartCount,
    36→    totalViews,
    37→    totalRecommendations,
    38→    subscription,
    39→    recentCharts,
    40→    widgetConfig,
    41→    recommenderConfig,
    42→    assignmentCount,
    43→    recentEventCount,
    44→  ] = await Promise.all([
    45→    db.sizeChart.count({ where: { shop } }),
    46→    db.sizeChart.count({ where: { shop, status: "active" } }),
    47→    db.sizeChart.count({ where: { shop, status: "draft" } }),
    48→    db.analyticsEvent.count({ where: { shop, eventType: "view" } }),
    49→    db.analyticsEvent.count({ where: { shop, eventType: "recommend" } }),
    50→    db.subscription.findUnique({ where: { shop } }),
    51→    db.sizeChart.findMany({
    52→      where: { shop },
    53→      orderBy: { updatedAt: "desc" },
    54→      take: 5,
    55→      select: {
    56→        id: true,
    57→        name: true,
    58→        category: true,
    59→        status: true,
    60→        updatedAt: true,
    61→      },
    62→    }),
    63→    db.widgetConfig.findUnique({ where: { shop } }),
    64→    db.recommenderConfig.findUnique({ where: { shop } }),
    65→    db.chartAssignment.count({ where: { shop } }),
    66→    db.analyticsEvent.count({
    67→      where: { shop, createdAt: { gte: sevenDaysAgo } },
    68→    }),
    69→  ]);
    70→
    71→  const plan = getPlan(subscription?.planId ?? "free");
    72→
    73→  // Onboarding steps
    74→  const hasChart = chartCount > 0;
    75→  const hasAssignment = assignmentCount > 0;
    76→  const hasWidget = widgetConfig !== null;
    77→  const hasRecommender =
    78→    recommenderConfig !== null && recommenderConfig.enabled;
    79→  const canUseAi = plan.limits.aiRecommender;
    80→
    81→  // Steps: install (always done), chart, assignment, widget, ai (only if eligible)
    82→  const onboardingSteps: Array<{ label: string; done: boolean }> = [
    83→    { label: "Install app", done: true },
    84→    { label: "Create first size chart", done: hasChart },
    85→    { label: "Assign chart to products", done: hasAssignment },
    86→    { label: "Customize widget", done: hasWidget },
    87→    ...(canUseAi
    88→      ? [{ label: "Enable AI recommender", done: hasRecommender }]
    89→      : []),
    90→  ];
    91→  const completedSteps = onboardingSteps.filter((s) => s.done).length;
    92→  const totalSteps = onboardingSteps.length;
    93→
    94→  // Chart limit usage for free plan
    95→  const chartLimit = plan.limits.maxCharts;
    96→  const chartsUsedPercent =
    97→    chartLimit > 0 ? Math.min(100, Math.round((chartCount / chartLimit) * 100)) : 0;
    98→
    99→  const recentChartsFormatted = recentCharts.map((c) => ({
   100→    ...c,
   101→    updatedAt: c.updatedAt.toISOString(),
   102→  }));
   103→
   104→  return {
   105→    shop,
   106→    chartCount,
   107→    activeChartCount,
   108→    draftChartCount,
   109→    totalViews,
   110→    totalRecommendations,
   111→    recentEventCount,
   112→    plan,
   113→    recentCharts: recentChartsFormatted,
   114→    onboardingSteps,
   115→    completedSteps,
   116→    totalSteps,
   117→    chartLimit,
   118→    chartsUsedPercent,
   119→    isNewUser: chartCount === 0,
   120→  };
   121→};
   122→
   123→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   124→// Component
   125→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   126→
   127→export default function Dashboard() {
   128→  const {
   129→    chartCount,
   130→    activeChartCount,
   131→    draftChartCount,
   132→    totalViews,
   133→    totalRecommendations,
   134→    recentEventCount,
   135→    plan,
   136→    recentCharts,
   137→    onboardingSteps,
   138→    completedSteps,
   139→    totalSteps,
   140→    chartLimit,
   141→    chartsUsedPercent,
   142→    isNewUser,
   143→  } = useLoaderData<typeof loader>();
   144→
   145→  const isFreePlan = plan.id === "free";
   146→  const isOnboardingComplete = completedSteps === totalSteps;
   147→  const progressPercent = Math.round((completedSteps / totalSteps) * 100);
   148→
   149→  return (
   150→    <s-page heading="Dashboard">
   151→
   152→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   153→      {/* Welcome Banner — new users only                                     */}
   154→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   155→      {isNewUser && (
   156→        <s-section>
   157→          <s-banner tone="info">
   158→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   159→              <s-heading>Welcome to Size Chart & Recommender</s-heading>
   160→              <s-paragraph>
   161→                Reduce size-related returns by up to 40% with beautiful size
   162→                charts and AI-powered recommendations. You're just a few steps
   163→                away from your first published chart.
   164→              </s-paragraph>
   165→              <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
   166→                <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
   167→                  Create your first chart
   168→                </s-button>
   169→                <s-button href="/app/pricing">View plans</s-button>
   170→              </s-stack>
   171→            </s-stack>
   172→          </s-banner>
   173→        </s-section>
   174→      )}
   175→
   176→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   177→      {/* Metrics Row — 4 cards                                               */}
   178→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   179→      <s-section heading="Overview">
   180→        <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
   181→
   182→          {/* Size Charts */}
   183→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   184→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   185→              <s-heading>{formatNumber(chartCount)}</s-heading>
   186→              <s-text>Size Charts</s-text>
   187→              <s-text tone="neutral">
   188→                {activeChartCount} active · {draftChartCount} draft
   189→              </s-text>
   190→            </s-stack>
   191→          </s-box>
   192→
   193→          {/* Chart Views */}
   194→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   195→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   196→              <s-heading>{formatNumber(totalViews)}</s-heading>
   197→              <s-text>Chart Views</s-text>
   198→              <s-text tone="neutral">
   199→                {recentEventCount} events in last 7 days
   200→              </s-text>
   201→            </s-stack>
   202→          </s-box>
   203→
   204→          {/* AI Recommendations */}
   205→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   206→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   207→              <s-heading>{formatNumber(totalRecommendations)}</s-heading>
   208→              <s-text>AI Recommendations</s-text>
   209→              <s-text tone="neutral">
   210→                {plan.limits.aiRecommender
   211→                  ? "Recommender enabled"
   212→                  : "Upgrade to unlock"}
   213→              </s-text>
   214→            </s-stack>
   215→          </s-box>
   216→
   217→          {/* Current Plan */}
   218→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   219→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   220→              <s-heading>{plan.name}</s-heading>
   221→              <s-text>Current Plan</s-text>
   222→              <s-text tone="neutral">
   223→                {plan.price === 0 ? "Free forever" : `$${plan.price}/month`}
   224→              </s-text>
   225→              {isFreePlan && (
   226→                <s-button href="/app/pricing" variant="primary">
   227→                  Upgrade
   228→                </s-button>
   229→              )}
   230→            </s-stack>
   231→          </s-box>
   232→
   233→        </s-stack>
   234→      </s-section>
   235→
   236→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   237→      {/* Onboarding Checklist                                                */}
   238→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   239→      {!isOnboardingComplete && (
   240→        <s-section heading="Getting Started">
   241→          <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   242→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   243→              <s-text>
   244→                {completedSteps} of {totalSteps} steps completed
   245→              </s-text>
   246→              <s-progress-bar
   247→                progress={progressPercent}
   248→                tone="success"
   249→              />
   250→            </s-stack>
   251→
   252→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   253→              {onboardingSteps.map((step) => (
   254→                <s-box
   255→                  key={step.label}
   256→                  padding="base"
   257→                  borderWidth="base"
   258→                  borderRadius="base"
   259→                  background={step.done ? "subdued" : undefined}
   260→                >
   261→                  <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
   262→                    <s-badge tone={step.done ? "success" : "neutral"}>
   263→                      {step.done ? "Done" : "To do"}
   264→                    </s-badge>
   265→                    <s-text tone={step.done ? "neutral" : undefined}>
   266→                      {step.label}
   267→                    </s-text>
   268→                  </s-stack>
   269→                </s-box>
   270→              ))}
   271→            </s-stack>
   272→          </s-stack>
   273→        </s-section>
   274→      )}
   275→
   276→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   277→      {/* Quick Actions                                                        */}
   278→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   279→      <s-section heading="Quick Actions">
   280→        <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
   281→
   282→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   283→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   284→              <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-100">
   285→                <s-text>Create Size Chart</s-text>
   286→                <s-text tone="neutral">
   287→                  Build from a template or start blank. Takes under 3 minutes.
   288→                </s-text>
   289→              </s-stack>
   290→              <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
   291→                Create Chart
   292→              </s-button>
   293→            </s-stack>
   294→          </s-box>
   295→
   296→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   297→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   298→              <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-100">
   299→                <s-text>Customize Widget</s-text>
   300→                <s-text tone="neutral">
   301→                  Control how your size chart appears in the storefront.
   302→                </s-text>
   303→              </s-stack>
   304→              <s-button href="/app/widget">Customize</s-button>
   305→            </s-stack>
   306→          </s-box>
   307→
   308→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   309→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   310→              <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-100">
   311→                <s-text>View Analytics</s-text>
   312→                <s-text tone="neutral">
   313→                  Track chart views, recommendations, and conversions.
   314→                </s-text>
   315→              </s-stack>
   316→              <s-button href="/app/analytics">
   317→                {plan.limits.analytics ? "View Analytics" : "Upgrade to Unlock"}
   318→              </s-button>
   319→            </s-stack>
   320→          </s-box>
   321→
   322→          <s-box padding="base" borderWidth="base" borderRadius="base">
   323→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   324→              <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-100">
   325→                <s-text>Configure AI Recommender</s-text>
   326→                <s-text tone="neutral">
   327→                  Let shoppers find their size from height, weight, and body
   328→                  type.
   329→                </s-text>
   330→              </s-stack>
   331→              <s-button href="/app/recommender">
   332→                {plan.limits.aiRecommender ? "Configure AI" : "Upgrade to Unlock"}
   333→              </s-button>
   334→            </s-stack>
   335→          </s-box>
   336→
   337→        </s-stack>
   338→      </s-section>
   339→
   340→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   341→      {/* Recent Charts                                                        */}
   342→      {/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */}
   343→      <s-section heading="Recent Size Charts">
   344→        {recentCharts.length === 0 ? (
   345→          <s-box padding="large-200">
   346→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   347→              <s-heading>No size charts yet</s-heading>
   348→              <s-paragraph>
   349→                Create your first size chart to help customers find their
   350→                perfect fit and reduce size-related returns by up to 40%.
   351→              </s-paragraph>
   352→              <s-button href="/app/size-charts" variant="primary">
   353→                Create your first chart
   354→              </s-button>
   355→            </s-stack>
   356→          </s-box>
   357→        ) : (
   358→          <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   359→            {recentCharts.map((chart) => (
   360→              <s-box
   361→                key={chart.id}
   362→                padding="base"
   363→                borderWidth="base"
   364→                borderRadius="base"
   365→              >
   366→                <s-stack direction="inline" gap="base">
   367→                  <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-100">
   368→                    <s-text>{chart.name}</s-text>
   369→                    <s-stack direction="inline" gap="small-100">
   370→                      <s-badge tone="neutral">{chart.category}</s-badge>
   371→                      <s-badge
   372→                        tone={chart.status === "active" ? "success" : "neutral"}
   373→                      >
   374→                        {chart.status === "active" ? "Active" : "Draft"}
   375→                      </s-badge>
   376→                      <s-text tone="neutral">
   377→                        Updated {formatDate(chart.updatedAt)}
   378→                      </s-text>
   379→                    </s-stack>
   380→                  </s-stack>
   381→                  <s-link href={`/app/size-charts/${chart.id}`}>Edit</s-link>
   382→                </s-stack>
   383→              </s-box>
   384→            ))}
   385→            <s-link href="/app/size-charts">View all charts</s-link>
   386→          </s-stack>
   387→        )}
   388→      </s-section>
   389→
   390→      {/* ================================================================== */}
   391→      {/* ASIDE — Plan Details                                                */}
   392→      {/* ================================================================== */}
   393→      <s-section slot="aside" heading="Plan Details">
   394→        <s-stack direction="block" gap="base">
   395→          <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-100">
   396→            <s-badge tone={isFreePlan ? "neutral" : "success"}>
   397→              {plan.name} Plan
   398→            </s-badge>
   399→            <s-text tone="neutral">
   400→              {plan.price === 0 ? "Free forever" : `$${plan.price}/month`}
   401→            </s-text>
   402→          </s-stack>
   403→
   404→          {isFreePlan && chartLimit > 0 && (
   405→            <s-stack direction="block" gap="small-200">
   406→              <s-text>
   407→                {chartCount} / {chartLimit} charts used
   408→              </s-text>
   409→              <s-progress-bar
   410→                progress={chartsUsedPercent}
   411→                tone={chartsUsedPercent >= 80 ? "caution" : "success"}
   412→              />
   413→              {chartsUsedPercent >= 80 && (
   414→                <s-text tone="caution">
   415→                  Almost at your chart limit. Upgrade for unlimited charts.
   416→                </s-text>
   417→              )}
   418→            </s-stack>
   419→          )}
   420→
   421→          <s-unordered-list>
   422→            {plan.features.map((feature, i) => (
   423→              <s-list-item key={i}>{feature}</s-list-item>
   424→            ))}
   425→          </s-unordered-list>
   426→
   427→          {isFreePlan ? (
   428→            <s-button href="/app/pricing" variant="primary">
   429→              Upgrade Plan
   430→            </s-button>
   431→          ) : (
   432→            <s-button href="/app/pricing">Manage Plan</s-button>
   433→          )}
   434→        </s-stack>
   435→      </s-section>
   436→
   437→      {/* ================================================================== */}
   438→      {/* ASIDE — Getting Started Links                                       */}
   439→      {/* ================================================================== */}
   440→      <s-section slot="aside" heading="Getting Started">
   441→        <s-unordered-list>
   442→          <s-list-item>
   443→            <s-link href="/app/size-charts">
   444→              Create a chart from templates
   445→            </s-link>
   446→          </s-list-item>
   447→          <s-list-item>
   448→            <s-link href="/app/widget">Customize widget appearance</s-link>
   449→          </s-list-item>
   450→          <s-list-item>
   451→            <s-link href="/app/recommender">
   452→              Enable AI size recommendations
   453→            </s-link>
   454→          </s-list-item>
   455→          <s-list-item>
   456→            <s-link href="/app/pricing">View plans & features</s-link>

FIX two files in the Size Chart & Recommender Shopify app. READ each file first, then apply targeted fixes.

## File 1: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.size-charts.tsx`

Fixes needed:
1. **Line ~444: `variant="secondary"`** — this is NOT a valid Polaris web component button variant. Remove it (default variant is fine) or change to `variant="tertiary"` for the Edit button. Valid variants: `primary`, `tertiary`, `plain`.
2. **Line ~424: `<strong style={{ fontSize: "14px" }}>`** inside `<s-link>` — remove the `<strong>` tag and `style`. Just use `<s-link>` directly with chart.name text.
3. **Template grid spacing** — reduce `gap: "12px"` to `gap: "10px"` and `padding: "16px"` to `padding: "12px"` on template cards for tighter layout.
4. **Filter section** — the "Category:" and "Status:" labels + selects work fine but reduce the gap. Change outer `gap="base"` to `gap="small-200"`.
5. **Chart card action buttons** — there are 4 forms in a row (Edit, Publish, Duplicate, Delete). The Edit is a link button and the others are form submit buttons. Make sure they're properly aligned. Currently they use `<s-stack direction="inline" gap="small-200">` which is fine.

## File 2: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Size Chart & Recommender/app/routes/app.size-charts.$id.tsx`

Fixes needed:
1. **Table cell padding** — change `padding: "10px 12px"` in table body cells to `padding: "8px 10px"` for tighter rows
2. **Assignment section margins** — the `marginTop: "16px", marginBottom: "16px"` on the assignments list is excessive. Change both to `12px`.
3. **Assignment add form** — change `marginTop: "16px"` to `marginTop: "12px"`
4. **The "Save the chart first, then add assignments" text** at bottom of assignment section — appears even when chart is NOT new and you can already add assignments. Move this inside the `{isNew && ...}` block or remove it. Only show the banner for new charts.
5. **Input focus styles** — the chart name input has focus styles with `boxShadow: "0 0 0 3px rgba(44,110,203,0.15)"`. This is fine but make it consistent — also add similar focus to the assignment value input and category select.

## Rules:

- Usage: "X / Y published" with progress bar (same style as dashboard)

### 1. Page Header
- Keep `<s-page>` with back button, Save primary action, Publish secondary action
- Add a status badge next to the heading showing Published/Draft

### 2. Chart Details Section
- Wrap the name input and category/status in a clean card container
- Name input: proper label styling (`fontWeight: 600, fontSize: "13px", color: "#202223"`), input with `borderRadius: "8px"`, focus state with blue border + subtle box-shadow
- Category select: same styling as name input
- Status: show as a styled badge (green for active, gray for draft)
- Make category and status on the same row with proper flex layout

### 3. Table Editor — THE HERO
This is the most important component. Make it polished:

**Toolbar above table:**
- Clean bar with: unit toggle buttons (styled like pills — selected = blue bg, unselected = gray border), row/column count text on the right
- Wrap in a subtle background strip

**Table itself:**
- Clean header row: `background: "#f6f6f7"`, bold column names, subtle borders `#e1e3e5`

- Remove column (x) button: subtle, appears on hover of header

- Remove row (x) button: subtle, red on hover
- Add row button at bottom: clean text button `+ Add row`
- Add column button: `+` in header, blue accent

**Key polish:**
- `border-collapse: collapse` on table
- Consistent border color `#e1e3e5`
- All cell inputs: no border, transparent bg, full width
- Table container: `border: "1px solid #e1e3e5"`, `borderRadius: "8px"`, `overflow: hidden`

### 4. Product Assignments Section  
- Clean card-style container
- Current assignments: each in a subtle row with type badge + value + remove button
- Empty state: "No assignments yet" in neutral text
- Add assignment form: inline select + input + button, all styled consistently
- New chart banner: clean info banner

### 5. Sidebar Preview — Make it feel like the actual storefront widget
- Wrap in a card with subtle shadow
- Header bar: chart name, styled like a widget header
- Table with clean read-only styling
- Footer: unit info + size count
- Overall: feels like a "phone mockup" preview of the widget

- Clean label-value pairs

The user wants me to analyze competitor screenshots and build the best possible Size Charts page. Let me study each competitor:

1. **Shopplaza** (Screenshots 1-2): Clean empty state with illustration, Import button, modal for import options
2. **Shopplaza Editor** (Screenshot 3-4): Template chooser with product type images (Clothing, Footwear, Jewelry), sub-categories (Men's Fashion, Women's Fashion), visual cards
3. **Mageplaza** (Screenshot 5-6): Tabs (Size chart, Position, Size recommendation), rich text editor, measurement image upload, preview on right side, unit conversion toggle, display position settings


4. **Kiwi Sizing** (Screenshot 7): Visual preset templates with colorful icons grouped by category (Blank, Men, Women, examples), search, dropshipping templates
5. **SmartSize** (Screenshot 8): Search bar, warning banner, clean empty state
6. **Another competitor** (Screenshot 9): Full editor with table, body measurement image, rich text, preview panel, unit toggle, product linking

The pattern across all these tools is clear: they prioritize clean onboarding with visual templates, organize options by category or gender, use tabbed editors for different aspects of size charts, and include live preview functionality. The most successful ones combine an intuitive empty state with quick-access templates and a powerful editor that handles measurements, positioning, and recommendations all in one place.

To compete, I need to build a list page with filtering and proper empty states, a template picker using clean icons instead of images, and a comprehensive editor with separate tabs for chart data, assignments, and settings—plus a live preview panel, unit conversion, and a better table editor overall. I'm going to deploy multiple agents to execute this in parallel after planning the architecture.

Primary target: merchants switching from Kiwi Sizing (bugs, slow support, hidden fees). 13→ 14→## Stack (Exact Versions — Never Deviate) 15→| Layer | Technology | Version | Notes | 16→|-------|-----------|---------|-------| 17→| Framework | React Router 7 | `@shopify/shopify-app-react-router` v1 | **NOT Remix** — imports from `react-router`, never `@remix-run/*` | 18→| UI | Shopify Polaris | v13+ via web components (``, ``, etc.) | Use Polaris web components as shown in template | 19→| App Bridge | `@shopify/app-bridge-react` | v4 | `useAppBridge()` for toasts, navigation, modals | 20→| Auth | `shopify.server.ts` | — | `authenticate.admin(request)` before ANY Shopify API call | 21→| Database | Prisma | v6 | SQLite (dev) / PostgreSQL (prod) | 22→| Language | TypeScript | Strict mode | Zero `any` types. # CLAUDE.md â Shopify App Multi-Agent Automation

> Drop this file in your Shopify app's root directory.
> This tells Claude Code how to behave as a multi-agent system.

---

## Project Type
Shopify Embedded App (Remix / Next.js)

## Agent System
This project uses a multi-agent pipeline. When given a task, Claude operates as
multiple specialized agents in sequence. Each agent produces an artifact file
that the next agent consumes.

## Master Commands

### `/build [description]`
Runs the FULL agent pipeline for a new page/feature:
1. Research â 2. Architect â 3. Design â 4. Build â 5. QA â 6. Review
Loops BuildâQA until tests pass. Loops through Review until approved.
Does NOT stop until production-ready.

### `/fix [description]`
Runs QA agent on existing code, then Builder to fix, then Review.

### `/redesign [page/component]`
Runs Design agent fresh, then rebuilds.

### `/review [page/component]`
Runs Review agent only for code review and compliance check.

---

## When I Say "Build [X]" â Do This Automatically:

### Phase 1: RESEARCH (do not skip)
Before writing ANY code, research:
- Search for 5+ competitor Shopify apps with similar features
- Document what they do well and poorly
- Identify Shopify Polaris patterns for this page type
- List must-have features vs differentiators
- Save findings to `.artifacts/[task]/research.md`

### Phase 2: ARCHITECT (do not skip)
Plan the complete technical architecture:
- Define all TypeScript interfaces and data models
- Design component tree with props for each component
- Plan API routes with input/output types and error cases
- Define state management strategy (server vs client vs URL state)
- Plan loading, error, and empty states
- Define build order
- Save to `.artifacts/[task]/architecture.md`

### Phase 3: DESIGN (do not skip)
Make every visual decision:
- Layout grid and visual hierarchy
- Component states (default, hover, focus, loading, error, empty)
- Exact colors (Polaris tokens + any custom)
- Typography choices
- Animation specs (duration, easing, properties)
- Responsive behavior for desktop/tablet/mobile
- All copy and microcopy (no placeholder text)
- Save to `.artifacts/[task]/design-spec.md`

### Phase 4: BUILD
Implement EVERYTHING:
- Follow architecture exactly
- Implement design spec pixel-perfectly
- No TODOs, no placeholders, no "implement later"
- Full error handling on every async operation
- All TypeScript types (no `any`)
- All loading states with skeletons
- All empty states with helpful CTAs
- All animations from design spec
- Full accessibility (ARIA, keyboard nav, focus management)

### Phase 5: QA
Test everything:
- Write unit tests for all utilities and hooks
- Write integration tests for all API routes
- Write component tests for all interactive components
- Write edge case tests (empty data, huge data, special chars, offline)
- Verify every component matches design spec
- Run accessibility audit
- If ANY test fails â go back to Phase 4, fix, and re-test

### Phase 6: REVIEW
Final quality check:
- Code review for patterns, naming, complexity
- Shopify App Store compliance verification
- Performance audit (bundle size, render time, API calls)
- Security audit (auth, XSS, CSRF, injection)
- If issues found â go back to Phase 4, fix, re-test, re-review

### DONE Criteria
A task is DONE only when:
- [ ] All 6 phases completed
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Review approved
- [ ] No TODOs in code
- [ ] No TypeScript errors
- [ ] No eslint warnings
- [ ] All states handled (loading, error, empty, success)
- [ ] Accessibility verified
- [ ] Mobile responsive verified

---

## Code Standards (apply to ALL code written)

### TypeScript
- Strict mode always
- No `any` types â use `unknown` and narrow
- Export interfaces for all component props
- Use discriminated unions for complex state

### React / Remix / Next.js
- Functional components only
- Custom hooks for reusable logic
- Proper Suspense boundaries
- Error boundaries around async sections
- Use Polaris components as base, extend with CSS modules

### Shopify Specifics
- Use authenticated session on all admin API routes
- Handle webhooks idempotently
- Implement GDPR endpoints
- Use App Bridge for embedded app navigation
- Follow Polaris design guidelines as baseline
- Use Shopify's latest stable API version (not "unstable")
- Minimal OAuth scopes

### File Organization
```
app/
âââ routes/
â   âââ app.[feature].tsx         # Route files
âââ components/
â   âââ [Feature]/
â       âââ [Component].tsx       # Components
â       âââ [Component].module.css # Styles
â       âââ index.ts              # Barrel export
âââ hooks/
â   âââ use[Feature].ts           # Custom hooks
âââ services/
â   âââ [feature].server.ts       # Server-side logic
âââ types/
â   âââ [feature].ts              # Type definitions
âââ utils/
    âââ [feature].ts              # Utility functions
```

---

## Important: Never Stop Early
When building a feature, NEVER:
- Stop after "the basic structure is in place"
- Leave placeholder text or TODO comments
- Skip loading/error/empty states
- Skip mobile responsiveness
- Skip accessibility
- Skip tests
- Present partial work as complete

ALWAYS work through ALL 6 phases for every task. The goal is PRODUCTION-READY code that can ship immediately.

# Shopify App Multi-Agent Automation Framework

## What This Is
A **multi-agent system for Claude Code** that automates building production-grade Shopify app features. Instead of manually prompting Claude step by step, you assign a task and 6 specialized agents work in sequence until the feature is production-ready.

## Agent Pipeline

## Setup (3 steps)

### Step 1: Copy agent files to your project
```bash
cp -r agents/ /path/to/your/shopify-app/agents/
cp -r scripts/ /path/to/your/shopify-app/scripts/
cp -r templates/ /path/to/your/shopify-app/templates/
cp -r checklists/ /path/to/your/shopify-app/checklists/
```

### Step 2: Add CLAUDE.md to your project root
```bash
cp PROJECT-CLAUDE.md /path/to/your/shopify-app/CLAUDE.md
```
Claude Code reads this file automatically and knows how to operate as the multi-agent system.

### Step 3: Start building
Open your project in Claude Code and say:
```
Build the Product Analytics Dashboard with sales trends, top sellers, 
low stock alerts, and conversion rates. Mobile responsive with skeleton 
loading states.
```

Claude will automatically run through all 6 agents.

## Usage

### Full Pipeline (recommended)
Just describe what you want in natural language:
```
Build the Settings page with general config, notifications, billing, 
integrations, and danger zone sections. Auto-save with toast confirmations.
```

### Shell Script (alternative)
```bash
./scripts/orchestrate.sh "Build the Product Listing page with filters and bulk actions"
```

### Single Agent

```

### Start from Specific Phase

# Skip research/architecture, just redesign and rebuild
./scripts/orchestrate.sh "Update the Orders page" --from=design

# Just re-test and re-review
./scripts/orchestrate.sh "Verify the Settings page" --from=qa
```

## Quick Start Prompts
See `templates/quick-start-prompts.md` for copy-paste prompts for common Shopify app pages.

## Customization
- Edit agent files in `agents/` to adjust behavior
- Edit `CLAUDE.md` (or `PROJECT-CLAUDE.md`) to change project-level rules
- Add checklists in `checklists/` for domain-specific requirements
- Modify `scripts/orchestrate.sh` to change the pipeline flow

## Key Features
- **Self-correcting**: QA failures loop back to Builder automatically
- **Review rejections**: Loop back to Architect for redesign if needed
- **Production quality**: No TODOs, no placeholders, no partial work
- **Full Shopify compliance**: Built-in App Store requirement checks
- **Competitor-aware**: Research agent studies real competitor apps
- **Design-first**: UI/UX decisions made before any code is written

# Setup Guide: Add Multi-Agent System to Your Shopify App

## 5-Minute Setup

### Step 1: Copy Files Into Your Project

# Navigate to your Shopify app root

## Agent System
This project uses a multi-agent pipeline. When given a task, Claude operates as
multiple specialized agents in sequence. Each agent produces an artifact file
that the next agent consumes.

## Master Commands

### `/build [description]`
Runs the FULL agent pipeline for a new page/feature:
1. Research â 2. Architect â 3. Design â 4. Build â 5. QA â 6. Review
Loops BuildâQA until tests pass. Loops through Review until approved.
Does NOT stop until production-ready.

### `/fix [description]`
Runs QA agent on existing code, then Builder to fix, then Review.

### `/redesign [page/component]`
Runs Design agent fresh, then rebuilds.

### `/review [page/component]`
Runs Review agent only for code review and compliance check.

## When I Say "Build [X]" â Do This Automatically:

### Phase 1: RESEARCH (do not skip)
Before writing ANY code, research:
- Search for 5+ competitor Shopify apps with similar features
- Document what they do well and poorly
- Identify Shopify Polaris patterns for this page type
- List must-have features vs differentiators
- Save findings to `.artifacts/[task]/research.md`

### Phase 2: ARCHITECT (do not skip)
Plan the complete technical architecture:
- Define all TypeScript interfaces and data models
- Design component tree with props for each component
- Plan API routes with input/output types and error cases
- Define state management strategy (server vs client vs URL state)
- Plan loading, error, and empty states
- Define build order
- Save to `.artifacts/[task]/architecture.md`

### Phase 3: DESIGN (do not skip)
Make every visual decision:
- Layout grid and visual hierarchy
- Component states (default, hover, focus, loading, error, empty)
- Exact colors (Polaris tokens + any custom)
- Typography choices
- Animation specs (duration, easing, properties)
- Responsive behavior for desktop/tablet/mobile
- All copy and microcopy (no placeholder text)
- Save to `.artifacts/[task]/design-spec.md`

### Phase 4: BUILD
Implement EVERYTHING:
- Follow architecture exactly
- Implement design spec pixel-perfectly
- No TODOs, no placeholders, no "implement later"
- Full error handling on every async operation
- All TypeScript types (no `any`)
- All loading states with skeletons
- All empty states with helpful CTAs
- All animations from design spec
- Full accessibility (ARIA, keyboard nav, focus management)

### Phase 5: QA
Test everything:
- Write unit tests for all utilities and hooks
- Write integration tests for all API routes
- Write component tests for all interactive components
- Write edge case tests (empty data, huge data, special chars, offline)
- Verify every component matches design spec
- Run accessibility audit
- If ANY test fails â go back to Phase 4, fix, and re-test

### Phase 6: REVIEW
Final quality check:
- Code review for patterns, naming, complexity
- Shopify App Store compliance verification
- Performance audit (bundle size, render time, API calls)
- Security audit (auth, XSS, CSRF, injection)
- If issues found â go back to Phase 4, fix, re-test, re-review

### DONE Criteria
A task is DONE only when:
- [ ] All 6 phases completed
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Review approved
- [ ] No TODOs in code
- [ ] No TypeScript errors
- [ ] No eslint warnings
- [ ] All states handled (loading, error, empty, success)
- [ ] Accessibility verified
- [ ] Mobile responsive verified

- Strict mode always

# Shopify App Store Compliance Checklist

## Authentication & Authorization
- [ ] Uses Shopify OAuth 2.0 flow correctly
- [ ] Session tokens validated on every authenticated request
- [ ] Handles token refresh automatically
- [ ] Minimal OAuth scopes (only what's needed)
- [ ] Handles shop uninstall webhook (cleanup data)

## Embedded App Requirements
- [ ] Uses Shopify App Bridge for navigation
- [ ] CSP headers configured for Shopify admin embedding
- [ ] No full-page redirects outside the Shopify admin
- [ ] Uses Polaris for consistent UI with Shopify admin
- [ ] Handles auth redirects without blank screens

## GDPR Compliance
- [ ] `POST /api/webhooks/customers/data_request` â returns customer data
- [ ] `POST /api/webhooks/customers/redact` â erases customer data
- [ ] `POST /api/webhooks/shop/redact` â erases shop data after uninstall
- [ ] All endpoints respond within 48 hours
- [ ] Privacy policy URL configured in app settings

## API Usage
- [ ] Uses dated API version (e.g., `2024-10`), not `unstable`
- [ ] Handles rate limits gracefully (429 responses)
- [ ] Implements retry with exponential backoff
- [ ] Batches API calls where possible (GraphQL bulk operations)
- [ ] No unnecessary polling â use webhooks for real-time data

## Webhooks
- [ ] Webhook handlers are idempotent (safe to replay)
- [ ] HMAC validation on all incoming webhooks
- [ ] Responds with 200 within 5 seconds
- [ ] Processes heavy work asynchronously (background job)
- [ ] Handles webhook delivery failures gracefully

## Billing (if applicable)
- [ ] Uses Shopify Billing API for charges
- [ ] Handles subscription creation, activation, cancellation
- [ ] Shows clear pricing before merchant approves
- [ ] Handles billing edge cases (declined, frozen, expired)
- [ ] Free plan or trial available

## Performance
- [ ] App loads within 3 seconds
- [ ] API responses under 500ms
- [ ] No blocking operations on the main thread
- [ ] Implements proper caching
- [ ] Lazy loads non-critical resources

## User Experience
- [ ] Clear onboarding flow for new merchants
- [ ] Empty states guide users to next action
- [ ] Error messages are helpful and actionable
- [ ] Loading states prevent confusion
- [ ] Accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- [ ] Works on mobile (merchants use phones)

## Security
- [ ] No secrets in client-side code
- [ ] Input validation on all API routes
- [ ] CSRF protection on mutations
- [ ] XSS prevention (sanitize rendered content)
- [ ] No open redirects
- [ ] Secure session storage

## Role
You are the REVIEW AGENT. You are the final gate before code ships. You do a senior-engineer-level code review, check Shopify App Store compliance, and verify everything is production-ready. You have VETO power.

**Architecture Review**

- Is the separation of concerns clean?
- Are there any god components doing too much?
- Is the data flow predictable and traceable?
- Are there any circular dependencies?

**Code Quality**
- Is naming consistent and descriptive?
- Are functions small and focused (< 50 lines)?
- Is complex logic well-commented with WHY (not WHAT)?
- Are magic numbers extracted to constants?
- Is error handling consistent across the codebase?
- Are types precise (no unnecessary `any` or overly broad unions)?

**React Patterns**
- Are hooks following rules of hooks?
- Is component composition used effectively (vs prop drilling)?
- Are expensive computations memoized appropriately?
- Are effects clean (proper deps, cleanup functions)?
- Are controlled vs uncontrolled inputs consistent?

**API Quality**
- Are all routes properly authenticated?
- Is input validation thorough?
- Are error responses consistent and informative?
- Are Shopify API calls batched where possible?
- Is rate limiting handled proactively?

- Check for unnecessary re-renders

- API calls are batched where possible
- Proper caching strategy is implemented

- [ ] All user input is sanitized
- [ ] CSRF protection on all mutations
- [ ] Session handling is secure
- [ ] No open redirects
- [ ] Rate limiting on public endpoints

- [ ] No console.log statements
- [ ] No commented-out code
- [ ] No unused imports
- [ ] No unused variables
- [ ] Error tracking integration ready (Sentry/similar)
- [ ] Logging is structured and useful
- [ ] Environment variables are documented
- [ ] Database migrations are reversible
- [ ] Feature flags for gradual rollout (if applicable)

## Process (Follow Exactly)

### Step 1 — Read the Rules
Read `CLAUDE.md`. Every rule is non-negotiable.

### Step 2 — Study Existing Patterns
Read `app/routes/app._index.tsx` and `app/routes/app.tsx` for the exact code patterns used in this project (Polaris web components, App Bridge, React Router 7).

### Step 3 — Plan Before Building
Answer these before writing code:
1. Route type? → `app.*` (admin) / `api.*` (public) / `webhooks.*` / component
2. Prisma models? → existing or new schema changes needed?
3. Data flow? → loader fetches → component renders → action mutates
4. Plan gating? → Free / Starter / Growth / Pro — which plan minimum?

6. AI component? → Does this involve recommendations/ML? If yes, involve ai-engine

### Step 4 — Database Changes (If Needed)
1. Read `prisma/schema.prisma` — understand current state
2. Add model/fields following existing conventions
3. Run `npx prisma migrate dev --name descriptive_name`
4. Run `npx prisma generate`
5. Flag the change — all agents need to know about schema changes

5. Error handling in every action
